instruction.text: Decide whether the statement is true or false.

atoms.a: The Supreme Court works as the judicial branch.
The House of Representatives cannot veto a bill proposed by the Senate.

wrong.text: The House and the Senate can both veto each other's bills.

atoms.a: The president functions as the executive branch.
Congress works as the U.S. judicial branch.

wrong.text: Congress works as the U.S. legislative branch.

atoms.a: The first-past-the-post electoral system resulted in a two-party system.
Congress' responsibilities include overseeing the law's accordance with the Constitution.

wrong.text: This is the Supreme Court's responsibility.

atoms.a: Even though only Congress can declare war, the President can order military operations.
The USA have a multi-party-system.

wrong.text: In practise, the USA has a two-party-system, even though other smaller parties exist.

atoms.a: The main political parties are the Democrats and the Republicans.
In the Midterm elections, most members of the Supreme Court are elected.

wrong.text: In the Midterm elections, most members of Congress are elected.

atoms.a: Midterm elections are held in the middle of a president's term.
The House of Representatives and the Senate have the same amount of members.

wrong.text: The House has a fixed total of 435 members, while the Senate consists of a total of 100 senators.

atoms.a: Congress can pass amendments to the Constitution.
The Supreme court cannot declare acts of Congress unconstitutional.

wrong.text: The Supreme court can declare both acts of Congress and presidential acts unconstitutional.

atoms.a: The president is elected every four years.
Democrats and Republicans have the same basic ideas about the Government's role.

wrong.text: They do not. Democrats emphasize stronger government regulation of markets, whereas Republicans advocate for reduced government regulation to promote free markets.

atoms.a: The president is elected directly by the people.

wrong.text: The president is elected indirectly through an Electoral College.

atoms.a: The amount of electors in a state depends on its population size.
Anyone can run for U.S. President.

wrong.text: Presidential candidates need to be at least 35 years old, be born in the USA and pay for their political campaigns themselves.

atoms.a: A newly elected president is inaugurated in January.
Revenue bills must originate in the Senate.

wrong.text: Revenue bills must originate in the House of Representatives.

atoms.a: Election Day for federal elections is always on the Tuesday following the first Monday in November.
